artworks.title: Achilles Fighting the River Gods Xanthus and Simois
artworks.description: Couder's Louvre decoration: Achilles against Scamander (Xanthus) and Simois — Iliad XXI as neoclassical flood and fury.

artworks.title: Achilles Pursued by the Xanthus
artworks.description: Schopin's canvas: the river-god Scamander rising in waves against Achilles — Romantic water overwhelming the hero until Hephaestus intervenes.

artworks.title: Fury of Achilles
artworks.description: Coypel's fury scene from the Trojan cycle — Achilles' rage that drives him into Scamander's flood in the Iliad's river battle.

artworks.title: Achilles Fighting the River-God Scamander
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum print from an Achilles life series: the hero locked with Scamander — the river of Troy personified as opponent.

artworks.title: Hephaestus and the Scamander
artworks.description: Illustration of Hephaestus' fire against Scamander's flood — the Iliad's elemental duel that saves Achilles from the river.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Book XXI — Scamander rises against Achilles until Hera sends Hephaestus' fire; the river of Troy as warrior.

popCulture.title: Scamander
popCulture.description: The god of Troy's river — Xanthus to the gods, Scamander to men — father of Teucer and foe of Achilles.
